rv.q: There’s no narrative as such: it’s a series of sketches that are often hilarious, sometimes moving and which gain a cumulative thematic power. It’s acted by a diverse five-strong cast with deeply funny bones, on a bare stage with a letterbox window at one end and a mural of rainbow inclusivity at the other.
Hussain's splatter gun approach to obvious societal evils makes some intriguing points but misses more than it hits.
An enjoyable short play, exploring the effect of words and language, that is both funny and thought provoking.
